memories.content: The user stores prepared meals on the second shelf of the freezer.
The user went to the market without a shopping list and bought onions that were already at home.
On a day the user shopped after checking a refrigerator photo, they did not make a duplicate purchase.
On a day the user made a spicy stew, they left part of one bowl uneaten.
The next time the user cooked it, they used half as much chili powder and finished the meal.
When cooking with their younger brother, the user assigned the cooking sequence only verbally and they did the same task twice.
The next time, the user and their younger brother split ingredient preparation and heat control and finished the meal 20 minutes earlier.
When cooking together, the user's younger brother prefers to divide the cooking and dishwashing roles in advance.
The local agent can compare responses across several meals, but it cannot conclude from one unfinished food item that the user dislikes that ingredient.
The condition of frozen prepared food may vary with its packaging and storage duration.
The user keeps four folding chairs for family barbecues in storage.
When six family members gathered in a noisy indoor restaurant, the user asked several times for the person across from them to repeat what was said.
The user held the next gathering in their father's yard and moved between seats while speaking with everyone.
On a day the user started the barbecue at midday, sunlight led them to finish the meal quickly.
The next time, the user started at 6 p.m. and remained outside until sunset.
Because the side dishes brought by the user's mother and older sister had no labels, the user opened the same container twice.
At the next gathering, the user wrote each food's name and who brought it on a small piece of paper.
After a barbecue, the user's younger brother prefers to divide leftover food into small containers to take home rather than discard it.
The local agent can summarize preparation and responses from prior family barbecues but cannot know the next attendees or weather.
The user's father's yard receives strong direct sunlight at midday; after 6 p.m., shade and wind lower the felt temperature.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate household practices: the reference centers on meal storage, shopping, cooking adjustments, collaboration, and inference limits, while the compared frame centers on barbecue logistics, setting, timing, labeling, leftovers, and forecasting limits. No claims govern the same operational decision closely enough for a cross-frame relation.
